title: Preston’s Jordan Thompson given three-game ban for kicking bottle that hit a fan
content:
Preston North End midfielder Jordan Thompson has been suspended for three matches after kicking a water bottle that struck a supporter.

Thompson was substituted in the 65th minute of Preston’s 2-0 defeat against Norwich City on Saturday. As he left the field and headed back towards the away dugout, he kicked a bottle into the stands at Carrow Road which hit a fan in the side of the head.

The 29-year-old held up his hand in apology after the incident, which was not seen by referee Gavin Ward. The Football Association subsequently alleged that the incident constituted violent conduct.

In a statement the FA said: “Jordan Thompson denied the charge against him, but an independent Regulatory Commission found it to be proven following a hearing and imposed the standard punishment of a three-match suspension for violent conduct.”

Thompson is now set to miss Preston’s Championship fixtures against Stoke City, Leicester City and Queens Park Rangers. Preston are 17th in the table, 10 points above the relegation zone with eight games remaining.

Thompson has made 16 appearances for the club since joining in the summer after his contract at Stoke expired. He did not make his debut for the side until November after undergoing ankle surgery before the season.

The Northern Ireland international came through the academy at Manchester United and has also played for Rangers and Blackpool.
